user.text: When navigating from the dashboard to a project, I want the project's title to appear instantly, but I don't want to prefetch the rest of the project page.

history.assistant:
Build succeeds. The route output confirms the change worked: `/projects/[slug]` is now `◐ (Partial Prerender)` — prerendered as static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content.

## What I changed

**`next.config.ts`** — enabled Partial Prefetching (requires the already-on `cacheComponents`):
```ts
cacheComponents: true,
partialPrefetching: true,
```

**`app/page.tsx`** — opted the dashboard links into per-link prefetching so the cached, URL-specific title resolves *before* the click:
```tsx
<Link href={`/projects/${project.slug}`} prefetch={true}>
  {project.name}
</Link>
```

**`app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`** — split the single `<Suspense>` into two boundaries:
- `ProjectTitle` — reads `params` and the cached `getProjectTitle` (`'use cache'`). With `prefetch={true}`, this resolves at prefetch time, so the `<h1>` renders the instant you click.
- `ProjectDetails` — calls `await navigation()` *before* `getProjectDetails`. Per the [Optimizing prefetching](node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/optimizing-prefetching.md) guide, awaiting `navigation()` above the work leaves it out of every prefetch, so the details are produced only on navigation and stream in behind their own fallback. `getProjectDetails` keeps its `"use cache"` lifetime below the call (awaiting `navigation()` inside a cached scope isn't allowed).

## Why this gives you exactly what you asked for

| Part | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Title | Cached + URL-specific → resolved by `prefetch={true}` → **instant on click** |
| Details/activity | Excluded from prefetch via `navigation()` → **streams in after navigation**, never prefetched |

Two things worth noting from the docs:
- A cold cache (first visit / after expiration) still requires the server to compute the cached title once, so the *first* navigation may briefly show the `Loading project...` fallback. Subsequent navigations are instant while the cache is warm.
- `prefetch={true}` costs one server invocation per visible link. With only two links here that's fine; if this dashboard grows into a large grid, consider a hover-triggered prefetch instead (see the [Prefetching guide](node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/prefetching.md#hover-triggered-prefetch)) so you only pay for links the user is likely to click.

18 	## What "instant" means
19 	
20 	A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.
21 	
22 	> **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait.
23 	
24 	A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `<Suspense>` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition.
25 	
26 	Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `<Suspense>` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout.
27

29 	<summary>Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI</summary>
30 	
31 	On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `<Suspense>` boundary in the full tree.
32 	
33 	On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger.

35 	This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load.

17 	[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route.
